actions.translateQuick: Translate these 3 to try it out

vault.title: Create your vault password
vault.why: Your provider keys are encrypted with it and never leave your control.
vault.openWhat: Open the vault form to choose a password for your vault.
vault.passwordWhat: Type a password here, then confirm with the button below.

unlock.title: Unlock your vault
unlock.why: Your provider keys stay encrypted until you unlock the vault.
unlock.openWhat: Open the vault form to enter your vault password.
unlock.passwordWhat: Type your vault password here, then confirm with the button below.

cloudVault.title: Create your vault and add a key
cloudVault.what: Choose a vault password, then add a key. For a quick test, create a free Google AI key. Already have a key for a supported provider? Choose "Use my own provider" first. You come back here when it is done.
cloudVault.why: Your provider keys are encrypted with your password and never leave your control. A key is how the AI provider knows it's you.

cloudUnlock.what: Unlock your vault on the vault page. You come back here when it is done.

cloudKey.what: Add a key on the vault page. For a quick test, create a free Google AI key. Already have a key for a supported provider? Choose "Use my own provider" first. You come back here when it is done.

key.title: Add a key to start translating
key.why: A free key lets NARN Freeway translate your game at no cost while you try it out. You can change the provider at any time in the project's Config tab.
key.whyOwn: Your {{provider}} key is how {{provider}} knows it's you. You can change the provider at any time in the project's Config tab.
key.choiceWhat: For a quick test, create a free Google AI key and paste it into your vault. Already have a key for a supported provider? Choose "Use my own provider".
key.pasteWhat: Paste the key here, type your vault password below, then save.

project.title: Bring in your game's text
project.why: NARN reads every entry and only translates what's missing.
project.createWhat: Give your project a name, then create it.
project.sourceWhat: Pick the language your text is written in.
project.targetsWhat: Tick the languages you want to translate into, or use Select all.
project.importWhat: Choose the CSV file you exported from your game editor.
project.confirmWhat: Check the summary, then confirm the import.

translate.title: Translate
translate.why: Freeway picks a suitable free model for each language automatically.
translate.whyOwn: {{provider}} translates this project with your own key.
translate.whyCustom: This project's routing, set up in Advanced, picks the provider for each entry.
translate.openWhat: Open the tab that lists your entries.
translate.quickWhat: 3 entries that still need translating are selected. Translate them to try it out, or translate everything now.
translate.fewWhat: Your entries are selected. Translate them now.
translate.nothingWhat: Your file already has a translation for every language you chose, so there is nothing to translate.
translate.nothingWhy: To add a language, tick it on the Data tab and save. Otherwise, go on to export your file.
translate.progressWhat: The translation is running. This line shows its progress.
translate.progressWhy: The tour continues when the translation has finished.

failed.title: The translation didn't go through
failed.why: The highlighted bar below shows what happened.
failed.authWhat: The provider rejected your key. Check the key, then try again.
failed.quotaWhat: The free quota is used up for now. Wait a little or add another key, then try again.
failed.quotaWhatOwn: {{provider}} refused for now: your account's quota or credit is used up. Check your plan with the provider, then try again.
failed.quotaWhatCustom: A provider in this project's routing refused for now: a quota or credit is used up. Wait a little or check the provider's plan, then try again.
failed.otherWhat: Nothing was translated. Check your key, then try again.

parked.title: The translation is paused
parked.what: Your translation is paused and waiting on the provider. Check your key, then stop this run and start a new one.

waiting.title: The translation is waiting
waiting.why: The highlighted bar below shows its status. The tour continues when the translation has finished.
waiting.quotaWhat: The free quota is used up for now. The translation resumes by itself when quota is free again.
waiting.modelWhat: The free models available right now are below the quality this run aims for. The translation resumes by itself when a better one is available.

rest.title: The test worked
rest.what: Your 3 test entries are translated into every language you chose. Translate the rest now, or export what you have.
rest.why: You can translate the rest later from the list of entries.
rest.skipped: The rest can wait. Download what is translated so far.

export.title: Export
export.why: Your game editor can import this file to bring the translations into your game.
export.openWhat: Go back to the tab where you imported your file.
export.downloadWhat: Download the translated file for your game editor.

closing.title: You're all set
closing.what: This is the simplified view: it shows only what you need to translate and export. Advanced has more tools. Flip the switch to Advanced for a short tour.
closing.whatAdvanced: You're using Advanced, which shows every tool. A short tour explains what each section is for.
closing.why: You can switch at any time from the top bar.

providerChoice.title: Use my own provider
providerChoice.description: Pick the provider you have a key for. It translates this project and the new projects you create. To combine several providers, switch to Advanced.
providerChoice.existingRouting: This project already has routing set up, so it stays as it is. You can change it in Advanced.
providerChoice.freeHeading: These have free keys. Picking one translates with it alone, without the other free models in the NARN Freeway pool.
providerChoice.switchedOff: {{provider}} is switched off in Advanced, so it was not used. Switch it back on in Global Config, or choose another provider.
providerChoice.waitingForKey: {{provider}} has no key in your vault yet, so NARN Freeway translates for now. Add its key, or choose NARN Freeway in the project's Config tab.
providerChoice.appliedCollab: {{provider}} now translates the projects shared with you.

guideTours.title: Tours

first-run.name: Guided first run
first-run.summary: Set up a provider, add your strings, translate and export, one step at a time.

advanced-sections.name: Advanced sections
advanced-sections.summary: What each tab and view that Advanced adds is for.

glossaries.name: Glossaries
glossaries.summary: Create a glossary, add terms and apply it, so key terms stay consistent.

routing.name: Routing
routing.summary: A 30-second look at how NARN picks who translates what.

quality.name: Quality
quality.summary: A short look at how NARN checks your translations.

compare.name: Compare
compare.summary: A short look at reviewing translations side by side.

review-translation-ai.name: AI review of translations
review-translation-ai.summary: A short look at having an AI check your translations.

orphans.name: Orphans
orphans.summary: See what happens to an entry your file leaves out, with a practice orphan the tour puts back.

guideTours.needsProject: Open a project to take this tour.
guideTours.switchedToAdvanced: Switched to Advanced mode for this tour.

confirm.title: Switch to Simple for the guided setup?
confirm.body: The guided setup is built for Simple mode, which hides the advanced tabs. You can switch back at any time from the top bar.

offer.title: New to Routing?
offer.body: A 30-second look at how NARN picks who translates what.

config.title: Routing picks who translates
config.what: This is where you choose which translation provider handles your strings.
config.why: Use it to send some languages or kinds of text to a different provider, or to keep one provider for everything.

mode.title: Simple or advanced rules
mode.what: Switch here between one provider for everything and a list of rules.
mode.why: Start simple. Move to rules when you want a different provider for a language, a category or a tone.

offer.title: New to Glossaries?
offer.body: A short look at keeping names and key terms consistent.

list.title: Your glossaries
list.what: Each glossary is a list of terms with the translation you want for each.
list.why: Terms such as character names or game jargon then come out the same way every time.

create.title: Start a glossary
create.what: Create an empty glossary and add your own terms to it.
create.why: Do this when you already know the words that must never be translated differently.

generate.title: Let AI suggest terms
generate.what: Ask an AI provider to find likely terms in your strings.
generate.why: It saves you reading the whole file to find them. You review and accept what it proposes.

offer.title: New to Quality?
offer.body: A short look at how NARN checks your translations.

title.title: Automatic quality checks
title.what: Every translation is checked against rules such as missing tags, changed placeholders and length limits.
title.why: Problems that would break your game show up here instead of in play-testing.

overview.title: Your pass rate
overview.what: This shows how many checks passed and how many failed across the project.
overview.why: A quick way to tell whether the translations are ready or still need work.

issues.title: The most common problems
issues.what: The kinds of problem that fail most often are listed here.
issues.why: Fixing the most common one first clears the most failures.

offer.title: New to Compare?
offer.body: A short look at reviewing translations side by side.

target.title: Pick the language
target.what: Choose which language to look at next to the source text.
target.why: Review one language at a time, line by line, and edit as you go.

reference.title: Add a reference language
reference.what: Show a second language alongside, such as one you read well.
reference.why: Useful when you cannot read the target language: you can check the meaning against a language you know.

translate.title: Translate from here
translate.what: Translate the rows you selected, or all rows that match your filters.
translate.why: Handy for filling gaps you spot while reviewing, without leaving this tab.

offer.title: New to AI review?
offer.body: A short look at having an AI check your translations.

intro.title: A second opinion on translations
intro.what: An AI provider reads your translations next to the source and scores them.
intro.why: It finds mistakes and awkward wording that automatic checks cannot, so you can fix them before shipping.

start.title: Review the last run
start.what: Start a review of the most recent translation run.
start.why: Reviewing just what was translated lately keeps the cost and the wait small.

all.title: Review everything
all.what: Review all translations in the project, not only the latest run.
all.why: Use it before a release, or after you changed the glossary or routing.

compare.title: Compare
compare.what: The source next to one target language, row by row, with an optional reference language.
compare.why: Review and edit one language carefully, even one you do not read.

routing.title: Routing
routing.what: Decides which provider translates each language, category or tone.
routing.why: Send each kind of text to the provider that handles it best.

stage-details.title: Stage details
stage-details.what: A stage's name, gameplay details and description, with their translations.
stage-details.why: Translate the text that describes a level, outside your string file.

quality.title: Quality
quality.what: The automatic checks every translation goes through, and the ones that failed.
quality.why: Catch broken tags, changed placeholders and text that is too long before you ship.

review-source-ai.title: Source AI review
review-source-ai.what: An AI provider reads your source text and points out typos and unclear wording.
review-source-ai.why: Better source text gives every language a better translation.

review-translation-ai.title: Translation AI review
review-translation-ai.what: An AI provider reads translations next to the source and scores them.
review-translation-ai.why: It finds wrong meanings and awkward wording that automatic checks miss.

review-manual.title: Manual review
review-manual.what: A queue of translations that need review, to approve, edit or flag one by one.
review-manual.why: Work through doubtful translations quickly, with keyboard shortcuts.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.what: Lists of terms with the translation you want for each.
glossary.why: Names and key terms then come out the same way every time.

category.title: Category
category.what: Groups strings by kind, such as UI labels, dialogue or item names.
category.why: Routing rules and batches can then treat each kind of text differently.

color-text.title: Text Styler
color-text.what: A drafting tool for text with colours, bold, italics and font sizes.
color-text.why: Write styled text without typing the markup by hand.

orphans.title: Orphans
orphans.what: Entries that disappeared from a later import, kept with their translations.
orphans.why: Nothing is lost when your file changes: link them back or delete them.

backup.title: Backup
backup.what: Packs the project into an archive you can download and restore.
backup.why: Go back to an earlier state if an import or a bulk change goes wrong.

sharing.title: Sharing
sharing.what: Invite collaborators and choose which languages each one may edit.
sharing.why: Translators work on their own languages, with their own AI providers.

global-config.title: Global Config
global-config.what: Settings for the whole workspace: providers, models and the credential vault.
global-config.why: Set up a provider once and use it in every project.

translation-memory.title: Translation Memory
translation-memory.what: Earlier translations, reused when the same text comes back.
translation-memory.why: It saves cost and keeps repeated lines translated the same way.

purpose.title: What a glossary is for
purpose.what: A glossary lists terms with the translation you want for each, such as character names or game jargon.
purpose.why: Translations then use your words every time instead of a new guess.

create.title: Create a glossary
create.what: Start a new, empty glossary here, or press Next to read on.
create.why: One glossary is often enough. Use more to keep sets of terms apart.

add-term.title: Add a term
add-term.what: Type the source term and its translation for each language, then add it.
add-term.why: Mark a term as constant when it must never be translated, such as a brand name.

assign.title: Apply it to this project
assign.what: An enabled glossary is used when this project is translated. Disable it to stop using it.
assign.why: Keep a glossary disabled while you are still building it.

effect.title: How it changes translation
effect.what: When a string contains a glossary term, the term and your translation of it are sent along with the string.
effect.why: The provider follows your choice instead of picking its own word.

generate.title: Let AI suggest terms
generate.what: Ask an AI provider to find likely terms in your strings.
generate.why: You review the suggestions and keep only the ones you want.

intro.title: What an orphan is
intro.what: An orphan is an entry that is missing from the last file you imported with Full replace.
intro.why: NARN keeps it here with its translations instead of deleting it, so nothing is lost by accident.

offer.title: Try it with a practice orphan
offer.what: The tour can turn one of your entries into an orphan for a moment, then put it back. Nothing is lost: the entry keeps its translations and returns to its place.
offer.why: A real orphan makes this tab easier to use later. Or let the tour just explain.

backup.title: Back up first
backup.what: A backup of the project is taken before the practice orphan is created. Nothing is lost either way: the tour puts the entry back.
backup.why: With a backup you can always return to this exact state from the Backup tab.

simulating.title: Creating the practice orphan
simulating.what: The tour imports your entries again without one of them. This takes a moment.
simulating.why: This is what happens when an entry disappears from a file you import with Full replace.

practice-row.title: Your practice orphan
practice-row.what: This entry is now an orphan. It no longer shows on the Translations tab, and its translations are kept.
practice-row.why: Orphans appear here after a Full replace import, so you can decide what to do with each one.

practice-options.title: What you can do with an orphan
practice-options.what: Relink moves its translations onto another entry, for example one whose text was only reworded. Delete removes it for good.
practice-options.why: Leave them alone for this one: the tour puts it back in the next step.

recover.title: Put it back
recover.what: Press “Put it back” and the entry returns to its place in the list, with its translations.
recover.why: The tour imports it again, the same way an entry comes back when your next file includes it.

restore.title: Your backup
restore.what: The backup taken before the practice is listed here. “Restore the backup” shows its Restore button; whether to press it is up to you.
restore.why: You don't need it: the entry is already back. Restore a backup only when something went wrong.

done.title: That's orphans
done.what: Orphans keep the entries and translations your last import left out, until you relink or delete them.
done.why: Have a look at this tab after each Full replace import.

explain-list.title: The orphans list
explain-list.what: Each orphan shows its source text and how many translations it keeps.
explain-list.why: The ones with the most translations come first: they are the most work to redo.

explain-options.title: Relink or delete
explain-options.what: Relink moves an orphan's translations onto another entry, for example one whose text was only reworded. Delete removes it for good.
explain-options.why: Relink when the text still exists in another form; delete when it is really gone.

notices.alreadyRecovered: The practice orphan is already back on the Translations tab.
notices.alreadyDeleted: The practice orphan was deleted, so the tour cannot put it back. If you took a backup, you can restore it from the Backup tab.
notices.otherProject: A practice orphan from this tour is still in another project. Switch to that project to put it back first.
notices.leftOut: The practice orphan is still in the Orphans tab. Press “Put it back” there to return it.

blocked.noEntries: There is no entry to practice with yet, so the tour only explains.
blocked.collaborator: Only the project owner can manage orphans, so the tour only explains.
blocked.sourcelessRows: Some entries have no source text, and an import cannot rebuild them exactly. The tour only explains, so nothing changes.
blocked.unsafeText: Some source text has a quote right before a comma or line break, which an import cannot rebuild exactly. The tour only explains, so nothing changes.
blocked.commaInSourceLabel: A source label has a comma or spaces at its ends, which an import cannot rebuild exactly. The tour only explains, so nothing changes.

errors.backup: The backup could not be created. Nothing was changed.
errors.simulate: The practice orphan could not be created. Nothing was changed.
errors.recover: The entry could not be put back yet. It is safe in the Orphans tab; try again.
errors.recoverRefused: The tour cannot put this entry back without changing other entries, so nothing was changed. Use Relink in the Orphans tab to move its translations, or restore the backup if you took one.
errors.load: Could not check on the practice orphan. Press “Put it back” to try again.

banner.text: This is the guided tour's practice orphan. Put it back to return it, with its translations, to the Translations tab.
banner.recovered: The practice orphan is back on the Translations tab.
